clue.text: Strong statement of intent from crossword compilers

definitions.text: statement of intent from crossword compilers
definitions.meaning: setters announcing 'we will set' a puzzle, contracted to we'll

explanation.surface: Crossword setters make a firm declaration of what they plan to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the entry as WE'LL SET: what a team of compilers would say about tomorrow's puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a well-built, solidly made person or object is described as strong.

clue.text: Maybe stone or white rocks round gulf

indicators.note: the shaken letters go around the single letter
rocking shakes the word white up so its letters move

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for gulf

explanation.surface: Stone, or perhaps pale rocks, lining a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe stone' looks like a rock but is a unit, 14 pounds in British use.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the stone is a British unit of mass, so it is one kind of heaviness measure.

clue.text: Sappers supporting desire for glory

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: lust is strong desire
RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers backing a craving for fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: radiance, distinction or splendour, as in adding lustre to a name.

clue.text: Thin binding weed — it's what's observed on road

indicators.note: the word for thin wraps around the other piece

parts.note: slim means thin
read as wee'd: urinated
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slender plant smothering a weed, which roadside verges must tolerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' is not a plant but the past tense of wee, to urinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the maximum legal pace motorists are meant to keep to on a highway.

clue.text: Perhaps member of school's right to be defended by solicitor

indicators.note: the single letter is shielded on both sides by the other word

parts.note: a tout solicits custom or sells tickets

explanation.surface: A pupil's legal right is defended by a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The school is a school of fish, and solicitor is not a lawyer but someone who solicits.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: fish swim in shoals called schools, and the river fish is one such member.

clue.text: Rot found in heart of beech trees

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of the five-letter beech

parts.note: a yew is an evergreen tree
an ash is a common deciduous tree

explanation.surface: Decay discovered at the core of a woodland of beeches.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'trees' covers two tree names in a row; the heart of a five-letter word is its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: rot in the sense of nonsense or humbug, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Record head of Amazon plugs can amuse

parts.note: to enter something is to record it in a log

indicators.note: the letter fills a gap inside the other word

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the opening letter of Amazon

explanation.surface: Log an Amazon order of plugs that may keep someone happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to keep people interested or diverted.

clue.text: Go out with someone you went out with one time

parts.note: a former partner, an ex
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Going out again with a former partner from way back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'went out' in the clue is dating, whereas the definition's 'Go out' means leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb: to leave a room or stage, to depart.

clue.text: Bond had fixed and sound returns

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rearranged, so the word had changes order
the word for sound comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: noise is sound

explanation.surface: James Bond had things put right, and noise came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' makes ADH from had; 'returns' gives ESION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sticking together, the tie or attachment that holds two things together.

clue.text: Devising something to wear with grand clothing feature

indicators.note: the two outer pieces dress the facial feature by surrounding it

parts.note: a hat is something worn
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Designing a costume piece that has a grand clothing detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like part of the fashion picture but is the container signal; 'feature' is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to plot or contrive, as in a scheme being concocted.

clue.text: Problem child? More than one!

definitions.meaning: a matter in dispute, a point of difficulty
offspring collectively, children, as in 'died without'

explanation.surface: A parent's question about a difficult child, answered with a sigh that there are several.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputed point is a problem; legal and old usage calls a person's children their offspring collectively.

clue.text: Tell me it's no longer popular and trendy

parts.note: a fashion that is out has passed its moment
with it means fashionable, up to date

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be told that a fad has passed and that something else is in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an impatient demand to speak up and reveal something, as in 'come on, say it'.

clue.text: Present way to improve home, framing art nouveau from parents

parts.note: here means in attendance, present

indicators.note: the home-improvement letters go around the rearranged art

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, home improvement done by the owner

indicators.note: French for new, so the word art is made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A home makeover with Art Nouveau touches, inherited from one's parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art nouveau' looks like the design style, but 'nouveau' (French for new) is the anagram signal for art, and 'framing' puts that inside the DIY letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something passed down from parents, by genes or inheritance, is described this way.

clue.text: What's possessed by wag — so hilarious!

definitions.text: What's possessed by wag — so hilarious!

indicators.note: the letters are held within the words that follow, straddling them

explanation.surface: A joker has a very funny quality, says an admiring friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for 'good sense of humour', used in lonely-hearts personal ads, sits across 'waG SO Hilarious'; a wag is a joker who has exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: Dating-ad shorthand for good sense of humour, the trait a witty joker plainly has.

clue.text: A Renaissance artist capturing utter mercenary

indicators.note: the painter's name takes in the other piece

parts.note: Albrecht Dürer, German Renaissance painter and engraver
to vent is to give voice to

explanation.surface: A Renaissance painter portraying a total hired soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' is a verb here, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a soldier of fortune who fights for pay; an adventurer in the old military sense.

clue.text: Philosopher and French writer with intimate, romantic works

parts.note: John Stuart Mill, English philosopher
George Sand, French novelist
boon as in boon companion, a close friend

explanation.surface: A list of a philosopher, a French novelist and a close friend, all writing passionate books.
explanation.walkthrough: Mills & Boon is a British publisher famous for mass-market romance novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The publisher's name stands for its romance novels, love stories sold in vast numbers.

clue.text: Look down during day — it's quite revealing

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

indicators.note: the drinking word goes within the abbreviated day

parts.note: WED is short for Wednesday
to neck a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: Looking downcast for a whole day can say a lot about someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is drinking, as in necking a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a dress or top cut to expose the throat and chest shows plenty of skin.

clue.text: Vehicle horse pulled back to marsh, initially

indicators.note: the words to and marsh come first in the entry

parts.note: taken as written
a bog is a marsh

indicators.note: the horse word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A cart that a horse dragged backwards towards a swamp at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal but only says which pieces come first, ahead of the reversed horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sledge for sliding down snowy slopes is a kind of conveyance.

clue.text: Qualifier of the year 2016 struggling for golf game

parts.note: 2016 was a leap year

indicators.note: the word for wrestles into a new order

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A competitor who qualified in 2016 is battling at golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges for into FRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a children's game of vaulting over a crouching player.

clue.text: Star briefly red and white, on repeatedly exploding

indicators.note: blown apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled
the little word on is used twice over

explanation.surface: A firework shows red and white flashes, bursting again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles on to ONON; with RED and WHITE these twelve letters are rearranged by 'exploding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a performer famous for a single hit, a celebrity only for a short while.

clue.text: No meat cut and stewed — recipe for person with beef

indicators.note: cooked up, so the letters are mixed together
trimmed, so the word meat loses its final letter

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin

explanation.surface: A meatless stew recipe for someone, odd since beef is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' turns meat into MEA, which 'stewed' rearranges with NO. Beef means complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a complainer, someone with a grievance; to beef is to grumble.

clue.text: Very solid cattle yard

parts.note: stock is livestock

explanation.surface: A farmyard holding cattle, built very sturdily.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: thickset and sturdy in build.

clue.text: Apologetic cry rings around the East End

indicators.note: in the area of London's East End the Cockney accent drops the initial H

parts.note: hoops are circular bands or rings

explanation.surface: An exclamation of sorry echoes through a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' here means in that neighbourhood, not encircling; the East End of London is where Cockneys drop their H's.
explanation.definitionFit: Interjection: what someone exclaims on making a small mistake, a quick sorry.

clue.text: Noble rebel and villain, fellow in the wrong

parts.note: a demon is a wicked person, a fiend

indicators.note: the fellow's letter is placed within the legal term

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who rose in revolt, and a wicked man, are both found to be at fault.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon de Montfort was the 13th-century English earl who led the barons' revolt against Henry III.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical example: an English earl who headed a rebellion of barons against the king.

clue.text: Love getting kiss on cheek and flower

parts.note: O is zero, love in tennis scoring
X is a kiss at the end of a letter
lip is insolence, cheek

explanation.surface: A lover receives a peck on the cheek and a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' is sauciness, not a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a primrose-family wild plant with yellow blooms.

clue.text: A slander's overthrown foreign parliament

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters are read upwards in reverse

parts.note: mud is slander, as in mud-slinging

explanation.surface: A defamation has toppled a parliament abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Russian legislative assembly, a parliament outside Britain.

clue.text: Art of 60s' dance music in large parties

indicators.note: the music style sits within the rearranged letters
used as a verb, to party: the word large goes wild and its letters are rearranged

parts.note: funk is a style of dance music

explanation.surface: The art scene of the sixties featured dance music at big parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is a first name, not painting: Art of Simon & Garfunkel, the 1960s duo. 'parties' is a verb making GAREL from large, with FUNK put 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the singer Art, half of the famous sixties folk-pop duo with Paul Simon.

clue.text: Be the manager in charge of ancient characters

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone takes on managing and being responsible for old letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for the letters of old Germanic alphabets, carved runes, used here as ancient characters.

clue.text: Return of tedious person with drink, but he won't get a round

indicators.note: the pair of words is read backwards, coming back

parts.note: a drag is a bore
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A bore comes back to the bar with a drink but never buys for the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns the bore and the drink around together; a round is drinks bought for the whole group.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun for a miser, a stingy person who avoids buying drinks for others.

clue.text: One side needs some light paint

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: One wall needs a little light-coloured paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to depict or represent in a picture or in words.
